Desmond Tutu - Health Update

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Desmond Tutu has been in hospital for two weeks. He has had prostate cancer since 1996/7 and underwent a number of successful treatments in the US. How is his health now?

Script:


INTRO
Trevor On Saturday, Arch Bishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu’s son Trevor, expressed his gratitude for the improvement in his fathers’ health after an operation earlier in the week.
Trevor Trevor: “He has come out amazingly well, far better than we could have seriously have hoped for.”
Lavinia Lavinia: “He is increasingly frail, but he says old age is not for sissy’s (laughs).”
Lavinia Lavinia Crawford-Browne his former personal assistant of 22 years joined with his inner Anglican community to pray for his health.
Ingrid Dr: “I saw him on Wednesday afternoon, the Arch had come out of theatre.”
Visuals of Ingrid le Roux For more than 30 years, Dr. Ingrid le Roux’s has been the Arch Bishop’s doctor.
Ingrid Dr: “He was cheerful, had a little bit of pain, but he said it was getting better.”
Claire link LINK: “St. Georges Cathedral is very important to Arch Bishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu because of his political and spiritual history with the church. And this is where he comes every Friday and gives a sermon. Unfortunately, this Friday, he couldn’t make it because he’s in hospital for a recurring infection.”
Dr le roux Dr. Le Roux expects her very headstrong patient to be back on his feet in no time.
Dr. Dr: “He’s gone home, and he will live with some support of his family, but live and ordinary, fairly active life.”
Intv tutu Tutu: “One of my chief weaknesses is that I love to be loved, which will surprise many people.”
Visuals that show the icon One thing that surprises no one is just how loved the Arch Bishop is. His bravery and strength during apartheid - always lightened by his playful spirit - were fundamental to seeing the country through to the 1994 elections.
Intv tutu – May 9, 1994 “Yay woohoo” (dancing while voting)
Lavinia Lavinia: “85 years we have been blessed to have Desmond Tutu as a leader.”
Claire Link LINK: “There has been confusion around Arch Bishop Tutu’s illness – he was diagnosed with prostate cancer in the mid 90’s, but has had unknown recurring infections over the last few years.”
Trevor Trevor says the infection was due to a catheter that became infected and needed to be removed. It’s been a big relief for his family.
Trevor Trevor: “To us it means that he won’t be as susceptible to those infections as he has been.”
Visuals of him Illness is not new for the Arch Bishop, Lavinia remembers an intensely personal sermon Tutu delivered immediately after his cancer diagnosis in 1996.
VERY EMOTIONAL BITE Lavinia: “4.05 The theme was that he wished to be remembered, that he loved and that he laughed. For all of us, that is a great lesson, that we don’t need big monuments, but we need people to remember us because we made a difference in their lives.”
trevor Trevor: “It has been really really well managed, you can imagine you don’t want to be the doctor that killed off bishop tutu.”
Dr le Roux Dr. Le Roux says his spirit isn’t slowing down at all.
Dr. Le Roux Dr. “I think he’s a very determined patient, he will get out of bed, he will just start walking, I think he will soon be with us on Friday mornings again.
Trevor: Trevor: “What you see if what you get, whether he’s on a stage in front of thousands, he still has the same humour. He’s just spending more in silent contemplation, and in reading and writing and prayer.”
Lavinia likes to think there's a little bit of Tutu in every one of us.
Lavinia Lavinia: “I would say he is the condensation of what it is to be fully human. AA45801 :45 he lives and breathes what it is to be a good human being.
4 minutes.



Promo 10 seconds: Arch Bishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu is known to the world as the spiritual leader that helped end apartheid. But at 85 and in hospital how is our beloved leader and what messages do those close to him want to share?


Promo 15 seconds: Our Beloved Arch Bishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu was this week back in hospital.

Lavinia: “He is increasingly frail, but he says old age is not for sissy’s (laughs) 1.37 AA456001
Those closest to the spiritual icon - friends and loved ones update us on his condition and ever positive spirit.


Promo 2 15 seconds: Arch Bishop Emeritus Desmond Tutuhas been in an out of hospital with an infection. How is the spiritual leader doing? We hear from those close to him.
Dr. “I think he’s a very determined patient, he will get out of bed, he will just start walking, I think he will soon be with us on Friday mornings again.

Ingrid le Roux Transcription
I saw him on Wednesday afternoon, the Arch had come out of theatre, and he was cheerful, had a little bit of pain, but he said it was getting better, he was really relieved that the operation was over, and he did great.
It doesn’t really have a direct connection to the prostate cancer, his prostate cancer is under control, but it was a small procedure to prevent the infections that he has had.
I think that from now on we hope that his recovery will be rapid, that he will soon be on his feet again, I think he’s a very determined patient, he will get out of bed, he will just start walking, I think he will soon be with us on Friday mornings again, he’s an amazing compliant patient, so he does exactly what you tell him as a doctor, a part of being a wonderful person.
With age, you ahve to adjust your lifestyle and maybe not be as active, as you know he isn’t travelling as much as he did before, but I think he wants to live as active a life as possible, in relationship to people that are very important for him, I think he will fight back and be on his feet, and active again in relation to his age.
He didn’t even need to go into ICU after his operation, he went straight back to an ordinary room, he does not need high care, he’s gone home, and he will live with some support of his family, but live and ordinary, fairly active life.
